gap: No result ChatGPT got says that, at maker-store prices on 2026-11-08, a 2 kWh station costs no more per watt-hour than a 1 kWh one: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max $879 / 2,048 Wh ≈ $0.43/Wh, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 $899 / 2,073.6 Wh ≈ $0.43/Wh, BLUETTI AC180 $499 / 1,152 Wh ≈ $0.43/Wh. That makes a 100 W emitter cost about $51 per hour of backup on either size, against about $118 per hour on the 288 Wh BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 ($289.99).
standout_why: I opened ChatGPT's cited pages. animalstart.com (smart thermostats) names Jackery and Goal Zero only as brands, with no models or prices; its one runtime figure is 100 W ≈ 5 h on 500 Wh. pets.co.uk (vivarium winter) names no power station, UPS or price and gives only a formula. ChatGPT's own cards had no source and some prices were wrong: the AC180 card showed $899, but that is BLUETTI's 'AC180+Charger 2' bundle, and the standalone is $499. It showed the DELTA 2 Max at $1,199 and $1,049, but EcoFlow lists $1,029. No result ChatGPT got compares price per Wh or per hour of heat.
decides: This supports picking a 2 kWh model for an overnight-plus-day outage with a 100 W ceramic heat emitter. The extra runtime costs no more per Wh, so the DELTA 3 Max ($879) or our Elite 200 V2 ($899, $20 more for 25.6 Wh more) beats buying 1 kWh. The DELTA 2 Max loses outright: same 2,048 Wh for $150 more. The 288 Wh class (Elite 30 V2) only makes sense for a small heat mat. Separate issue: our page says the AC180 is 'Back late Nov', but BLUETTI's store showed it available at $499 today, so the stock cell needs updating.
